filename: Computing Extreme Storm Surges in Europe Using Neural Networks.pdf
title: Computing Extreme Storm Surges in Europe Using Neural Networks
code_availability: The software that we developed to train and evaluate the models is publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/Timh37/surgeNN) and archived in a Zenodo repository (Hermans, 2025; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14670781).
testbed_rationale: The study provides a well-defined benchmark framework comparing LSTM, ConvLSTM, MLR, and the hydrodynamic GTSM model for coastal surge emulation from reanalysis/climate-model predictors, with open-source code and data repository promised upon revision.
pain_points: Severe data imbalance: extreme storm surge events are heavily underrepresented relative to moderate conditions, causing standard MSE-trained models to underestimate extremes.
Temporal frequency trade-offs: models trained on 3-hourly data (to match climate model frequency) experience reduced performance compared to hourly hydrodynamic models.
Extreme underestimation: even with cost-sensitive density-based weighting, the neural networks predominantly underestimate the highest extremes (>99.9th percentile).
High sensitivity to spatial and non-atmospheric processes: at specific locations (e.g. Alicante), missing physical predictors (waves, coastal setup, river discharge) cause poor generalization.
extraction_notes: The data underlying the study is stated to be released on Zenodo upon final publication.
